business-domain-context

Bunkai domain map

What Bunkai is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Target repo: upex-bunkai-tms.

Overview

Confidence: Medium. The product shape is confirmed in code (schema and routes); the positioning prose comes from the target's own docs and was not independently verified.

Bunkai is a Test Management System (TMS) built as a Next.js app on Supabase (package.json). Its distinguishing idea is that the data model forces QA structure: an ATC cannot exist without a User Story and at least one Acceptance Criterion (atcs.user_story_id not null, atc_acceptance_criteria join in 0004_atcs.sql), a Test is an ordered chain of ATCs (test_steps, 0024_tests.sql), and a Bug must belong to a Module (bugs.module_id not null, 0046_bugs.sql).

Target users, as enforced by the code: members of a Workspace with roles viewer, member, admin or owner (workspace_members.role); external AI agents and CI pipelines that act through a Personal Access Token against /api/v1. Runs can be executed by a human, an agent or CI (runs.executor_mode).

Value delivered today: authoring (modules, stories, acceptance criteria, ATCs, tests), execution (runs with per-step results and evidence), defect tracking inside the QA loop, reporting (coverage, traceability, defect heatmap, recovery cycle, run history and flakiness), plus notifications, team chat, Jira import and Stripe billing.

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
Multi-tenant workspacesEvery test needs cross-workspace isolation checks (RLS); several migrations are named after 404-versus-403 cross-workspace behaviour
Tiered plans and seatsPlan limits and the billing grace period change what a workspace may do; test each tier
Structural traceabilityNegative tests: an ATC without a story or AC must be refused
Three execution modesRun behaviour differs for human, agent and CI executors; automated submission has its own idempotent path

Workspace

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Workspaceworkspace, workspace_idWorkspace (UI label from components/workspaces, not re-verified per string)workspaces, workspace_members0001_tenancy.sql

Business meaning: the multi-tenant root. A team's account; it owns Projects, members, billing plan and chat. Members hold a role (viewer, member, admin, owner) and a status (active, invited, suspended).

UI labels: UI action labels seen in code: "Create workspace".

Related terms: Project, Personal Access Token, Billing Plan.

Structure: attributes and lifecycle (invites, deletion, export) belong to business-data-context; that map was not generated yet, see discovery-gaps.

Project

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Projectproject, project_id, slugProject; action "Create project"projects0002_projects_modules.sql

Business meaning: the container, inside a Workspace, of Modules, Stories, ATCs, Tests, Runs, Bugs, Test Plans, Milestones and Environments.

Related terms: Workspace, Module, Environment.

Structure: see data map (not generated yet).

Module

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Modulemodule, module_id, pathModulemodules0002_projects_modules.sql

Business meaning: a node in a feature tree of at most six levels (CHECK modules_path_depth_max_6) that partitions a Project's features. It is a first-class entity, not a folder: coverage rollups and the defect heatmap aggregate by Module, and every Bug belongs to one. Archiving a module cascades to its subtree (archived_at, 0014); it can be moved, renamed and restored.

Related terms: Project, User Story, Bug.

Structure: see data map (not generated yet).

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
User Story (US)user_story, user_story_id, external_idUser Story; badges "Draft" / "Ready to test"; action "Mark ready to test"user_stories0003_authoring.sql

Business meaning: a requirement inside a Module, optionally linked to a Jira key (external_id, external_url). It has one or more Acceptance Criteria and a two-value gate, status in draft or ready_to_test, signalling that its criteria are settled enough to author ATCs.

Abbreviations: US.

Business meaning: one testable behaviour of a User Story, ordered by position. ATCs bind to ACs through atc_acceptance_criteria; an AC with no bound ATC is "uncovered".

Abbreviations: AC.

ATC (Acceptance Test Case)

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
ATCatc, atc_id, slug, @atc in KATA codeATC; action "Create ATC"atcs, atc_steps, atc_assertions0004_atcs.sql

Business meaning: the unit of authorship: a complete mini-flow with ordered steps (content, input data, expected) and assertions, bound to at least one Acceptance Criterion of a User Story. It is versioned (version), tagged, has a layer (UI, API, Unit) and an execution status (pass, fail, blocked, skipped, running, unrun). Editing an ATC propagates to every Test that chains it. Since 0087 it also has an optional technique and priority. ATC means Acceptance Test Case, not "atomic test component".

Abbreviations: ATC; ATP (Acceptance Test Plan) is a different, methodology term.

Related terms: Acceptance Criterion, Test, Run, Bug.

Structure: see data map (not generated yet). Value sets are in enumerations.

Test

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Testtest, test_idTest (a Test cannot be called "test case"; that word is the ATC)tests, test_steps0024_tests.sql

Business meaning: an ordered chain of ATCs (test_steps.atc_id, position) that is run as one unit. Title is 1 to 200 characters. It has tags (reserved suite tags: smoke, sanity, regression) and an automation status.

Related terms: ATC, Run, Test Plan.

Structure: see data map (not generated yet).

Run

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Runrun, run_id, executor_modeRun; actions "Start run", "Finish run"runs, run_atcs, run_steps, run_step_attachments0031_runs.sql

Business meaning: one execution of a Test against an Environment. It snapshots the Test title, ATC titles and step text at start, so later edits do not rewrite history. It ends passed, failed or aborted; steps carry notes and image evidence. Three status grains exist: run, chain position, step (see enumerations).

Related terms: Test, Environment, Bug.

Structure: see data map (not generated yet).

Bug

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Bug (defect)bug, severity P1..P4Bug; actions "New bug", "Report bug"bugs0046_bugs.sql

Business meaning: a defect recorded inside the QA loop, anchored to a Module and optionally to the Run, run step and ATC where it was found. Severity P1 to P4; status moves open, in progress, resolved, closed. Docs say the status moves one stage forward at a time, enforced procedurally, not by a CHECK.

Related terms: Module, Run, ATC.

Personal Access Token

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Personal Access Token (PAT)access_token, scopesTokens (Settings)access_tokens, access_token_secrets0008_access_tokens.sql

Business meaning: a bearer credential for the CLI and AI agents, issued and revoked in Settings. Scopes are limited to atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. It acts as the issuing member and cannot exceed that member's rights.

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Import Job; Jira connection; Tracker settingsimport_jobs, sync_stateJira (Settings)import_jobs, workspace_jira_connections, project_tracker_settings0019_import_jobs.sql, 0119

Business meaning: a workspace stores one Jira site connection; an Import Job asynchronously pulls Jira issues into a Project (status queued, running, completed, failed); only one active job per project (0020). Discovery gaps

  • Structure pointers: business-data-context is still a placeholder, so every term- section's Structure line points at a map that does not exist yet. Run project-context mode data.
  • Executor naming drift: the glossary says Execution Mode is manual | automated; the schema says runs.executor_mode is human | agent | ci. The team and the code name it differently.
  • Priority shipped: the glossary marks ATC Priority as not yet shipped (BK-399); migration 0087 adds atcs.priority and atcs.technique. Confirm the UI exposes them.
  • Milestone aggregation: the glossary says Test Plan aggregation is not built; migration 0112_milestone_plans.sql exists. Confirm what the UI shows.
  • UI labels: only a few action labels were verified in component strings (Create ATC, Create project, Create workspace, Start run, Finish run, Report bug, New bug, Mark ready to test). No i18n bundle was found; other labels are marked "not re-verified" and need a walk through the staging UI.
  • Bug severity wording: P1..P4 meaning (names such as critical or high) is not defined in the schema; check the UI or PRD.
  • Revenue figures: prices, licence (Apache or MIT), legal entity and cost structure are not in code; docs mark them as pending.
  • Market context: competitors and positioning (.context/business/market-context.md) were not verified against code.
  • Glossary-only terms: Command Palette, Flakiness signal, Recovery Cycle, Defect Heatmap and Coverage vocabulary are described in the legacy glossary; reports exist in migrations (0049, 0052, 0099) but no term- section was written for them. Consider adding on refresh.
  • Database not inspected live: the dbhub MCP failed to connect; everything is from migrations, which may lag the deployed schema.
